title: Extraction and Purification of Glycosaminoglycans from Scyliorhinus canicula
author: Talmoudi, Ghariani, et al.
materials: In this study, 20 g of cartilage powder are suspended in 200 ml of 0.1 M sodium acetate buffer, 5 mM EDTA, 5 mM cysteine-HCl, pH 6. The enzymatic treatment is carried out by adding 80 mg of papain (Sigma -Aldrich, St. Louis, MO). The preparation is thoroughly mixed and then incubated for 24 h at 65 °C (optimal temperature for papain activity). Digestion is stopped by denaturing the enzyme at 100 °C for 10 min. The removal of the protein residues was carried out by centrifugation (Hettich 380R centrifuge, max speed 1500 rpm, made in Germany) and NaCl (2%) is added to the supernatant. Indeed, a sufficient concentration of salt was necessary for complete precipitation of the polysaccharides.

GAGs extracts were filtered through a membrane (Wathman 4 kDa) to remove salts and low molecular weight materials. The filtrates were then further purified and dialyzed (dialysis tubing cellulose membrane avg. flat width 33 mm, SIGMA-ALDRICH) against deionized water for 24 h at 4 °C, to provide crude polysaccharide fraction after removal of contaminants which persisted after filtration. A second dialysis was performed for 24 h after replacement of the dialysis water. The purified GAG solutions were lyophilized in a CHRIST type lyophilizer (Alpha 2–4 LDplus) until a completely dried material is obtained.

Quantitative High-Performance Liquid Chromatography is performed on HPLC (Waters) with UV-visible detector, using an XTerra column RP18, 5 μm, 4.6*250 mm. Chemicals used were from Sigma-ALDRICH, Carlo Erba and LOBA Chemie. Ultrapure HPLC grade water was prepared using a Millipore purification system. All solutions should be freshly prepared.

The LC buffer and the mobile phase were prepared as reported elsewhere [22]. The buffer is composed of triethylamine and orthophosphoric-acid in ultrapure water (10/8 to 100 ml). The mobile phase was composed of buffer and acetonitrile (5/40 to 1000 ml); 0.5 g octanesulfonic acid are added to this solution; pH 4 was regulated with buffer components including triethylamine and 85% orthophosphoric-acid. The solution is filtered through a 0.45 μm Millipore filter before use. Washing phase should be sonicated.
Wcont: weight of standard of CS in mg.
Wtest: weight of sample of CS in mg.

steps.title: Prepare cartilage powder
steps.instruction: Obtain cartilage from fish heads, grind it and dry the material until a fine powder with low moisture content is obtained.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion of cartilage
steps.instruction: Suspend 20 g cartilage powder in 200 ml 0.1 M sodium acetate buffer containing 5 mM EDTA and 5 mM cysteine‑HCl, adjust pH to 6, add 80 mg papain (Sigma‑Aldrich), mix thoroughly and incubate for 24 h at 65 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add cartilage powder to buffer and adjust pH to 6.

steps.title: Terminate digestion and precipitate polysaccharides
steps.instruction: Denature papain by heating the mixture at 100 °C for 10 min, centrifuge at a maximum of 1500 rpm to remove protein residues, then add NaCl to the supernatant to a final concentration of 2 % (w/v) to promote polysaccharide precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Add NaCl to 2 % (w/v) in the supernatant.

steps.title: Filter and dialyze GAG extracts
steps.instruction: Filter the supernatant through a 4 kDa membrane, dialyze the filtrate against deionized water for 24 h at 4 °C, replace the dialysis water and dialyze a second 24 h, then lyophilize the purified GAG solution until completely dry.

substeps.instruction: Dialyze against deionized water 24 h at 4 °C.
Replace water and dialyze another 24 h.

steps.title: TCA and ethanol precipitation (Fraction I & II)
steps.instruction: Divide the dialyzed GAG solution into two aliquots; to one add TCA to 7 % (v/v) and incubate 24 h at 4 °C, then centrifuge to remove proteins. To both aliquots add two volumes of 99 % ethanol, keep at 4 °C for 24 h, centrifuge at 9000 rpm for 30 min at 4 °C and collect the sediments as Fraction I (with TCA) and Fraction II (without TCA).

substeps.instruction: Add TCA (7 % v/v) to first aliquot; incubate 24 h at 4 °C.
Add 2 volumes of 99 % ethanol to both aliquots; incubate 24 h at 4 °C.
Centrifuge at 9000 rpm for 30 min at 4 °C.
Collect sediments as Fraction I (TCA) and Fraction II (no TCA).

steps.title: Alkaline hydrolysis for total GAGs (Fraction III)
steps.instruction: Treat the enzymatically digested material with 2 M NaOH, adjust to pH 9 and incubate for 24 h at 40 °C (no TCA), then recover the precipitated polysaccharides as Fraction III.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 M NaOH to reach pH 9.
Recover the resulting GAG fraction (Fraction III).

steps.title: Prepare LC buffer and mobile phase
steps.instruction: Prepare buffer by mixing triethylamine and orthophosphoric acid in ultrapure water (10 mL triethylamine + 8 mL orthophosphoric acid per 100 mL water). Prepare mobile phase by mixing the buffer with acetonitrile (5 mL buffer + 40 mL acetonitrile per 1000 mL total), add 0.5 g octanesulfonic acid, adjust pH to 4 with triethylamine and 85 % orthophosphoric acid, filter through a 0.45 µm Millipore filter and sonicate the washing phase.

substeps.instruction: Mix triethylamine and orthophosphoric acid (10/8) in ultrapure water to 100 mL.
Combine buffer with acetonitrile (5/40) to 1000 mL.
Adjust pH to 4 using triethylamine and 85 % orthophosphoric acid.

steps.title: Prepare and inject HPLC samples
steps.instruction: Make standards and sample solutions at 75 % (w/v) concentration in the mobile phase, sonicate until completely dissolved, filter through a 0.45 µm filter, equilibrate the HPLC system for 30 min, inject standards before samples, and detect at 200 nm UV.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 75 % (w/v) standard and sample solutions in mobile phase.

steps.title: Calculate chondroitin sulfate content
steps.instruction: Use the formula %CS = (Atest / Acont) × (Wcont / 20) × (100 / Wtest) × 100, where Atest is the peak area of the sample, Acont the peak area of the standard, Wcont the weight of the standard (mg) and Wtest the weight of the sample (mg).
